topic: The Trinity of Logic: Ternary, Towers, and Triangles
target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science or Mathematics students

sections.title: Foundation: The Power of Three (Ternary)
lecture_lines: Binary uses two states, but ternary uses three.
Ternary digits represent states zero, one, and two.
Positional values are powers of three: one, three, nine.
Three-state switches generate twenty-seven unique configurations.
This base-3 system coordinates our entire logical map.
animations: Fade in the title 'The Power of Three (Ternary)' in #FFFFFF at the top center.

Display three circles labeled 0, 1, and 2 accompanied by the switches icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/switches.svg]. Sequentially highlight 0 in #00FF00, 1 in #FFFF00, and 2 in #FF0000.
Show magnitude labels: 3^2, 3^1, and 3^0 in #00FFFF arranged horizontally.
Place digits '2', '1', and '0' under labels. Show the calculation 2*9 + 1*3 + 0*1.
Transform the ternary digits into decimal '21' and flash it in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Rule Change: Constrained Towers of Hanoi
lecture_lines: Standard Hanoi allows moves between any two pegs.
Restricted rules only permit moves between adjacent pegs.
To reach peg two, disks must pass through one.
animations: Show three vertical pegs labeled 0, 1, and 2 in #FFFFFF. Place an orange disk (#FF8C00) [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg] on Peg 0.
Draw a red 'X' (#FF0000) over the direct path from Peg 0 to Peg 2 to show it is forbidden.
Animate the disk [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg] moving from Peg 0 to Peg 1, then from Peg 1 to Peg 2, following green arrows (#00FF00).

sections.title: Mapping States to Geometry
lecture_lines: Represent each valid disk configuration as a vertex.
Connect configurations reachable by a single legal move.
For two disks, states group into three clusters.
Connecting these clusters forms a larger triangular structure.
The final graph maps every possible puzzle state.
animations: Plot 3 dots in a horizontal line (#00FFFF) labeled 0, 1, and 2. Connect with white lines.
Arrange 3 copies of this line into a triangular formation. Label groups by Disk 2's position.
Draw white edges connecting the corners of these three groups to form a larger triangle.
Highlight a specific vertex and display the corresponding disk configuration on pegs in a small window.
Fade out labels and highlight the resulting 9-vertex graph structure in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Emergence of the Sierpinski Triangle
lecture_lines: Adding more disks expands the state-space graph recursively.
Two disks form three connected triangles of states.
Increasing disks reveals the iconic Sierpinski Triangle fractal.
Corners represent all disks stacked on a single peg.
The fractal structure perfectly captures the game's logic.
animations: Scale down the 9-vertex graph and triplicate it to construct the 3-disk state space.
Connect the three groups with new edges to complete the Sierpinski Triangle in #FFD700.
Label the three outermost corners as '000', '111', and '222' in #FF00FF.
Zoom into one corner to show the self-similar recursive structure within the fractal.
Pan out to reveal the full 27-state Sierpinski gasket representing 3 disks.

sections.title: Fractal Traversal via Ternary Addresses
lecture_lines: Ternary numbers act as addresses for every puzzle state.
Solving the puzzle means traversing the fractal's edges.
The longest path follows the triangle's outer perimeter.
animations: Trace a bold green path (#00FF00) from corner '000' to corner '222' along the fractal boundary.
Update a ternary counter on screen from 000 to 222 as the path progress.
Display the text 'Puzzle Solved' in #FFFFFF along with the puzzle icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/puzzle.svg] as the path reaches the final corner.
